title: 7Q Mechanism Map  -  Physics Instantiation

canonical_node.axiom: Every claim must be processed through the seven invariant questions (Q0 - Q7) to determine its truth score, with the mechanism never changing across domains; only the vocabulary adapts.
definitions: Q0 Posture Check: Determines whether the investigator is in advocacy or puzzlement mode; advocacy flags bias but does not kill the claim.
Q1 Identity: Fixes the object's entity type, physics type, formalism, master equation variable, and symmetry pair to prevent identity drift.
Q2 Location: Fixes the domain, subdomain, scale, regime, and isomorphism status (ISO-CONFIRMED, ISO-PARALLEL, ISO-ANALOGY) to prevent context drift.
Q3 Assertion: Pins the claim type, precision level, certainty, and physics-specific fields; must be precise enough to negate.
Q4 Evidence: Three-channel evidence (PS  CF) that multiplies; zero in one channel kills the score.
Q5 Dependencies: Analyzes the dependency chain to identify hidden assumptions and the axiom floor.
Q6 Consequences: Maps predictions into confirmed, untested, decisive, or failed categories.
Q7 Falsification: Names kill conditions using five universal death types and domain-specific kill conditions.
Truth Score: T = mean(S, E, L, D, P, C) where S=Survivability, E=Evidence, L=Logic, D=Dependencies, P=Predictions, C=Coherence.
derivation: The document defines the 7Q mechanism as a universal invariant for claim evaluation.
Each question (Q0 - Q7) has an invariant function and domain-specific vocabulary.
The truth score is computed as the mean of six variables derived from the answers to Q0 - Q7.
The mechanism is claimed to be domain-independent: 'The mechanism never changes. The vocabulary does.'
canonical_node.action: When any claim enters the system, apply Q0 - Q7 in order, compute the truth score, and output a verdict (ALIVE, DEAD, or OPEN) based on the score and kill conditions.
boundary: Does not provide a formal proof of the mechanism's correctness.
Does not specify the exact formulas for PS and CF in the evidence channel.
Does not define how to compute S, E, L, D, P, C precisely beyond the mean formula.
Does not list all possible domain-specific kill conditions for every field.
Does not claim that the mechanism is complete or that it guarantees truth.
test: For any claim, verify that each of Q0 - Q7 is answered with the defined vocabulary.
Check that the claim can be negated (Q3 test).
Verify that kill conditions are named and testable (Q7).
Compute the truth score and compare to the confidence level table.

dg1_dependencies: The document depends on the existence of a claim to evaluate.
It depends on the definitions of the seven questions and their invariant functions.
It depends on the truth score formula and the confidence level thresholds.
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a structured, domain-adaptable framework for evaluating claims across physics and other fields, with explicit kill conditions and a truth score.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the invariant core of the 7Q mechanism: the seven questions and the truth score formula remain unchanged across domains.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If the 7Q mechanism is removed, there is no systematic method for evaluating claims, leading to ad-hoc analysis and potential bias.
dg5_translation_registers: Physics vocabulary: entity types, physics types, formalisms, master equation variables, symmetry pairs.
Domain-specific subdomains, scales, regimes, and isomorphism statuses.
Claim types, precision levels, certainty levels, and physics-specific fields.
Kill conditions: five universal death types and domain-specific conditions.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Adopt as a structured heuristic for claim evaluation, but do not treat as a proven or complete method.

overstatement_risks: Claims that the mechanism is 'complete' or 'universal' without formal proof.
The truth score formula is presented as objective but lacks precise definitions for its components.
The document implies that the mechanism can determine truth, but it only provides a heuristic score.
kill_conditions: If the truth score formula is shown to be inconsistent or arbitrary.
If the mechanism fails to handle a known class of claims.
If the evidence channels (PS and CF) are not defined precisely enough to be computed.
risk.lean_target: A formal specification of the 7Q mechanism with precise definitions for all components, and a proof of its effectiveness or a clear statement of its limitations.

plain_summary: This document describes a seven-question framework (Q0 - Q7) for evaluating claims, with a truth score computed from six variables. It is designed to be domain-adaptable, but it is not formally proven and lacks precise definitions for some components. It should be treated as a structured heuristic, not a definitive method.
